categories.title: Second Temple Jewish Literature
categories.notice: Ancient Jewish literature useful for understanding the world surrounding the New Testament. Inclusion does not imply scriptural authority.

categories.title: Ancient Historians and Philosophers
categories.notice: Ancient witnesses whose accuracy, proximity, perspective, and purposes vary.

categories.title: Early Christian Literature
categories.notice: Early Christian writings outside the New Testament, useful for studying the beliefs and practices of some early communities.

categories.title: Lost and Disputed Works
categories.notice: Reference guides distinguishing works named in Scripture from later books using similar titles.

items.title: 1 Enoch
items.date: Composite work, approximately third century BCE to first century CE
items.description: An influential collection of Jewish apocalyptic writings concerning the Watchers, judgment, heavenly journeys, wisdom, and restoration.
items.edition: R. H. Charles translation, first published 1917
items.purpose: To explain the origin and judgment of evil powers, call the righteous to faithfulness, and offer hope that God will finally judge wickedness and restore creation.

items.title: Jubilees
items.description: A retelling of Genesis and part of Exodus arranged around jubilees, with particular attention to covenant, calendar, purity, and Torah.
items.edition: R. H. Charles translation, first published 1902; 1917 series edition
items.purpose: To retell Israel’s earliest history through covenant, calendar, purity, and Torah, presenting Israel’s way of life as established from creation.

items.title: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs
items.description: Testamentary speeches attributed to Jacob’s sons, combining ethical instruction, apocalyptic expectation, and a complicated textual history.
items.purpose: To place ethical warnings, calls to repentance, and future hope into farewell speeches attributed to Jacob’s twelve sons.

items.title: Life of Adam and Eve
items.date: Ancient Jewish work preserved in multiple later forms
items.description: Traditions expanding the lives of Adam and Eve after their expulsion from Eden, surviving in differing Greek, Latin, Armenian, Georgian, and Slavonic forms.
items.purpose: To expand the biblical account of Adam and Eve after Eden and reflect on repentance, death, temptation, and hope after humanity’s fall.

items.title: Psalms of Solomon
items.description: A collection of Jewish psalms reflecting on sin, foreign rule, righteous leadership, judgment, and messianic hope.
items.edition: G. Buchanan Gray in R. H. Charles, 1913
items.purpose: To interpret national crisis through prayer, condemn corrupt rulers and sinners, encourage the righteous, and express hope for God’s just Messiah.

items.title: 4 Ezra
items.description: An apocalypse wrestling with Jerusalem’s destruction, divine justice, Israel’s suffering, and hope for restoration.
items.purpose: To wrestle with how God can be just after Jerusalem’s destruction and to offer apocalyptic hope for Israel’s future restoration.

items.title: 2 Baruch
items.date: Late first or early second century CE
items.description: A Jewish apocalypse responding to Jerusalem’s destruction through visions, dialogue, lament, judgment, and restoration.
items.purpose: To help faithful Jews understand Jerusalem’s destruction, endure grief, remain obedient, and hope for judgment and restoration.

items.title: Flavius Josephus
items.description: Jewish historian and participant in the revolt against Rome. Principal works include Jewish War, Antiquities, Life, and Against Apion.
items.purpose: To preserve and interpret Jewish history for Jewish and Greco-Roman audiences, explain the revolt against Rome, and defend the antiquity and character of the Jewish people.

items.title: Philo of Alexandria
items.description: Alexandrian Jewish philosopher and interpreter whose writings illuminate diaspora Judaism, biblical interpretation, philosophy, and the first-century world.
items.purpose: To interpret the Torah for an educated Jewish and Greco-Roman world, showing how biblical faith, moral formation, and philosophical reasoning could be understood together.

items.title: Tacitus
items.description: Roman senator and historian whose Annals and Histories provide an elite Roman perspective on the early imperial period.
items.edition: Alfred John Church and William Jackson Brodribb translation, 1869
items.purpose: To investigate Rome’s emperors, wars, and political life, exposing how ambition, fear, corruption, and resistance shaped imperial power.

items.title: Suetonius
items.description: Roman biographer whose Lives of the Caesars preserves traditions about the emperors and imperial administration.
items.edition: Alexander Thomson translation, revised by T. Forester
items.purpose: To preserve biographical portraits of Rome’s rulers through their ancestry, careers, habits, virtues, faults, sayings, and reported omens.

items.title: Didache
items.date: Commonly dated to the late first or early second century CE
items.description: An early Christian church manual addressing the Two Ways, baptism, fasting, prayer, communal meals, teachers, and community order.
items.purpose: To give early communities practical instruction for moral conduct, baptism, fasting, prayer, communal meals, traveling teachers, and church order.

items.title: 1 Clement
items.date: Commonly dated near the end of the first century CE
items.description: A lengthy letter from the church at Rome to Corinth concerning division, humility, order, repentance, and communal peace.
items.purpose: To urge the Corinthian believers to end division, restore rightful leadership, practice humility, and recover peace and order.

items.title: Shepherd of Hermas
items.description: An early Christian collection of visions, commandments, and parables centered on repentance, moral formation, and the community.
items.purpose: To call Christians to repentance and moral faithfulness through visions, commandments, and symbolic parables about the life and judgment of the church.

items.title: The Biblical Book of Jashar
items.description: A lost work named in Joshua 10:13 and 2 Samuel 1:18. No surviving book can presently be identified securely as this biblical source.
items.status: Reference guide planned; no surviving text
items.purpose: Its original purpose is unknown because the work is lost; the surviving biblical references suggest it preserved poetic or heroic traditions remembered in ancient Israel.

items.title: Later Books Called Jasher
items.description: Several later works use the title Jasher or Sefer haYashar. They must not be presented as though they were demonstrably the lost work mentioned in Joshua and Samuel.
items.purpose: Purposes vary by work; these later compositions retell biblical history or offer moral teaching, but they should not be confused with the lost source cited in Joshua and Samuel.

items.title: Book of the Wars of the LORD
items.description: A lost work cited in Numbers 21:14. The biblical quotation survives, but the larger source does not.
items.status: Reference guide planned; no surviving text
items.purpose: Its original purpose is unknown because the work is lost; Numbers preserves only a brief poetic citation that appears connected with Israel’s journeys and victories.

items.title: Other Lost Works Mentioned in Scripture
items.description: A future guide to works such as the Acts of Solomon and writings associated with Nathan, Gad, Shemaiah, Iddo, and Jehu, carefully separating biblical references from later identifications.
items.purpose: Their individual purposes cannot be established from the surviving references alone; they appear to have preserved royal, prophetic, or historical records known to biblical writers.
